title: Post-Soviet pylons
description: Soviet-era pylon designs are shared by Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Baltic states and set them apart from the rest of Europe: plain barrel pylons, asymmetrical pylons that are not very tall with wide crossarms that do not taper outwards, A-shape pylons and concrete or steel H-frames. They do not help between these countries, but over time you get a feel for them. In Lithuania almost all H-frames are concrete; a steel one points to Latvia or Estonia instead. A-shape pylons are slightly more common here than in the other Baltic states.
